findings.desc: Canonical scope path classification is not actually shared with the prewrite guard. scope-contract.ts now uses classifyScopePath and recognizes lifecycle/runtime artifacts via lifecycle-registry and runtime-artifact-registry, but prewrite-guard.ts still keeps its own pathMatchesPattern/isInAllowedList/evaluatePathAgainstContract rule set and never consults those registries. Repro: a pure-function comparison on local dist with a minimal enforce contract returns scope pass and no violations for .lattice/story/actives/B-scope/summary.json and .lattice/activity.jsonl, while evaluatePathAgainstContract returns out_of_scope for both; src/in-scope.ts passes both. This violates CHK-001 adversarial intent that scope checks, guard paths, and operator-facing scope messages consume the same classifier/table, and would deny registered lifecycle/runtime writes under native-pretool or dispatch pre-apply even though the scope gate says they are allowed provenance/runtime artifacts.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by replacing prewrite-guard.ts ad hoc path matching with the shared classifyScopePath/pathMatchesScopePattern classifier. Verified lifecycle artifact .lattice/story/actives/B-scope/summary.json and runtime artifact .lattice/activity.jsonl no longer resolve as out_of_scope in prewrite guard smoke; protected/excluded/unknown behavior remains enforced. Commands passed: npm --prefix packages/main run build; node packages/main/dist/tasks/prewrite-guard-smoke.js; node packages/main/dist/tasks/scope-contract-smoke.js; node scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs.
